messages:
acme_ops: Hey, quick escalation — we ran a bulk delete for ~1.2k user records yesterday but customer reports they still appear in search results. Ticket #34567. Can someone confirm deletion pipeline + whether KMS key rotation or exports could keep objects visible? We're on eu-west region. cc @sara_support

sara_support: Sorry for the delay, looking now. Can you paste one example object_id and the account id? Also confirm if you applied a custom retention policy or used the account default.

acme_ops: object_id: obj_9f3b2a7c, account: acme-6442. We used the dashboard bulk-delete UI (deleted via UI job). No legal hold was set on the account AFAIK. Example API we used (UI triggers):
```
POST /v1/objects:delete 
{ "account": "acme-6442", "ids": ["obj_9f3b2a7c", "obj_..."], "mode": "soft" }
```

retention-bot: Policy snapshot for account acme-6442: custom_retention_days=180, legal_hold=false, last_policy_change=+7m. (automated)

ben_infra: I can take this. I see the delete job completed and tombstones were written to object-storage for the batch that contains obj_9f3b2a7c. However the search index still has the document live — looks like the index-eviction job for that partition failed on first attempt due to a transient timeout.

ben_infra: repro steps I ran:
1) GET /internal/storage/status?object_id=obj_9f3b2a7c -> status: tombstoned
2) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <infra-token>" https://search.internal.redwood/acme-6442/_doc/obj_9f3b2a7c -> returns 200 + doc

ben_infra: quick log snippet:
```
2026-03-16T22:12:04Z delete-job[worker-4]: wrote tombstone obj_9f3b2a7c to s3://redwood-storage/acme-6442/tombstones/2026-03-16/
2026-03-16T22:12:12Z index-evict[evict-2]: ERROR: partition-sync-timeout for acme-6442-p2
```

liam_security: On the KMS side — rotation completed last week (key v3). Rotation doesn't keep objects visible by itself. One thing to check: there was an export job for acme-6442 on Mar 15 that took a storage snapshot for compliance export. If a snapshot/export was created before deletion, the exported copy would still contain those records. Do we have evidence of an export?

retention-bot: Audit events for acme-6442: export_job export-logs-20260315 initiated by acme_ops at 2026-03-15T18:03Z, status: completed, export_id: exp_88a3.

maya_legal: acme_ops — did you request any data export or handoff to legal around Mar 15–16? If so that explains why copies still exist in an export bundle and those are outside normal delete lifecycle until we remove them.

acme_ops: We did run an export for a compliance handoff on Mar 15, yes. That export was delivered to their SFTP and we deleted the local export file afterward. We assumed deletion would remove records everywhere.

sara_support: Two parallel possibilities then: (A) search index shows stale docs due to failed index-evict (ben will trigger manual eviction), (B) an export snapshot contains records and remains retrievable by customer from the export destination. We'll confirm both.

ben_infra: Action: I ran a manual index-evict for partition acme-6442-p2 and restarted the eviction worker. I also queued a forced-sync for the search cluster. ETA for index to reflect deletions: ~20–30 minutes. Status: in-progress :hourglass_flowing_sand:

liam_security: I've pulled the export metadata. The export bundle exp_88a3 is a downstream copy — we don't auto-delete third-party exports. If customer still has the exported file, that file will contain the deleted rows. We can provide a checklist to confirm where the exported copy resides and options to rotate/revoke access to the SFTP.

acme_ops: Understood. Customer confirms they still have the exported CSV at their SFTP and used it to repopulate a search index on their side. So the source of truth was the export. In parallel please confirm the main index is cleaned so nobody else sees them.

sara_support: Thanks — two things: 1) ben, confirm index eviction completed; 2) liam, provide SFTP revocation steps and whether we can force-expire export links.

ben_infra: Confirmed — manual eviction completed; search queries now return 404 for obj_9f3b2a7c. I validated via the internal query and a sample search endpoint:
```
curl "https://search.redwood.com/acme-6442/_search?q=obj_9f3b2a7c" -> 0 hits
GET /v1/objects/obj_9f3b2a7c -> 404 tombstone
```
All good on our side. I'll follow up with an RCA for why the eviction worker timed out (likely transient network to internal metadata service).

liam_security: For the export: steps to lock it down — revoke SFTP creds on the customer's SFTP endpoint (we can't revoke a copy they control). If we had provided a pre-signed URL, we can expire it; confirm export delivery method. Also to close the loop: no HSM/KMS retention policy prevented deletion — the exported copy is the reason records are still accessible.

maya_legal: For records management: we need to make explicit in documentation + the export UI that exports are out-of-band and customers are responsible for downstream retention. Also adding a checkbox in export flow that warns about copies. I'll open a docs + product ticket.

acme_ops: Thanks everyone. Customer will purge their exported file and rotate their SFTP creds. Can we get the deletion verified in writing for their compliance team?

sara_support: Yes — I'll attach forensic proof in the ticket #34567: timestamped storage tombstone entries, index eviction logs, and audit events showing delete + export. Expect the package in ~2 hours. Marking this thread resolved once customer confirms export purge. :white_check_mark:

ben_infra: I'll include the eviction logs and the internal trace id: trace=evict-20260316-77b9.

liam_security: I'll add the export metadata (exp_88a3) and guidance on SFTP credential revocation into the response bundle.

acme_ops: Closing loop: customer confirmed removal of exported CSV and rotated credentials. Thanks — closing on our end. :thumbsup:

sara_support: Closing thread, attaching artifacts to ticket #34567. If anything reappears pls reopen.
